pr_title: Revert commit "Add a namespace label to admission metrics and expand histogram range to 0-10s"
pr_body:
/kind bug

**What this PR does / why we need it:**

By adding a namespace label to admission metrics we found that prometheus will be overwhelmed with out of memory errors within seconds due to amplified cardinality issues. This caused OOMs, raised memory usage in Prometheus from ~1,5GiB RAM steady usage to ~8GiB RAM usage (note, this is for OpenShift).

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes:**

Fixes #104008

**Special notes for your reviewer:**

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**

Revert addition of Add a namespace label to admission metrics and expand histogram range to 0-10s

```release-note
Fixes a 1.22 regression adding namespace label to admission metrics (and histogram exansion) due to cardinality issues.
```

issue_context.title: apiserver_admission_controller_admission_duration_seconds_bucket is very large in 1.22
issue_context.body:
#### What happened:
Running a 1.22 beta and the standard e2e test suite, we found that apiserver_admission_controller_admission_duration_seconds_bucket grew very large, very quickly.  Large enough to lead to instability as our monitoring stack repeatedly read them.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/101208#discussion_r679200100 looks like a prime candidate.  We are attempting a revert locally to see if it improves the situation.

#### What you expected to happen:
While we could technically work around this by passing non-default flags to the kube-apiserver, the defaults should be safe for use by non-experts.

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):

#### Anything else we need to know?:

#### Environment:
- Kubernetes version -- 1.22 beta-something pretty close to now-ish
- an openshift branch we're trying to integrate
comments: @deads2k do we have a k/k revert open yet for testing?
@ehashman I submitted https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/104033: let me know if this looks good to you.

review_comments: Was the issue the namespace label addition or the extra buckets?
we didn't identify, but the additional buckets for sure amplified the cardinality issue even more. mostly the namespace label is the biggest cardinality contributor.
How many series in total did you observe this added?
It was the churn from e2e tests. They basically create namespaces on a per-test basis.
We even have a test which creates 100 namespaces and deletes them.
